topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by reviewing prior concepts and defining the learning objectives centered on cancer evolution, cell of origin, and microenvironments.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms in clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how intrinsic genetic mutations and chromatin-level epigenetic alterations confer selective advantages that drive clonal expansion.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchies and cell of origin in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and investigate the cellular origin of tumors using experimental evidence from leukemia and colorectal systems.

topics.label: Microenvironmental cues, inflammation, and stromal support in tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how external factors such as inflammation, paracrine cytokines, and supportive stromal interactions are essential to promote and sustain malignant growth.

topics.label: Experimental and computational tools for analyzing tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic surveys sequencing technologies, spatial omics, and computational algorithms applied to investigate clonal dynamics and tumor-microenvironment interactions.

topics.label: Integrated framework of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the multi-factorial interplay among accumulated mutations, cell-of-origin plasticity, and microenvironmental pressures into an overall model of cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture and provides a brief look ahead to the next session on therapy.
